summary: Payette NF Cold Mountain lookout (Idaho County): tower built 1935 with a cabin and privy; tower moved in 1994 to private land at Payette Lake near McCall, where its top 20 feet were restored.

facts.design: 72-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 metal cab; log cabin and privy at the original site
facts.status_note: Tower removed from the original site in 1994; the top 20 feet were restored on private land at Payette Lake near McCall, Idaho. No source describes what remains at the original site today.

staffing.status: Norman Borlaug (1937, per NHLR); Leonard Rowland (1939, per firelookout.com); no full staff list in the sources read

access.note: Tower is on private property at Payette Lake, owned by Richard Holm, Jr.; do not visit without permission. The original site lies in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness (HABS); no public access to it is described in the sources read.

facts.agency: Payette National Forest (original site); tower now privately owned, administered by Richard Holm, Jr. (NHLR)

events.note: Privy built in 1934 at the original site (HABS). Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1934 for the tower and cabin; HABS dates the tower to 1935
Tower built at the original site (HABS); NHLR also says built in 1935
Log cabin built; NHLR says 1936 and HABS says 1936-37
NHLR says Norman Borlaug staffed the tower the year after the cabin was built
Tower disassembled and removed from the original site under a contract beginning August 1, 1994 (HABS); moved to private property near McCall (Idaho Fire Lookouts)
HABS documentation dated April 1996 found the privy and log cabin still standing at the original site
Log cabin burned in a wildfire, per NHLR
A private party restored the top 20 feet of the tower near the shore of Payette Lake (NHLR); Forest Lookouts gives the same year
Registered January 2, 2008 as US 714, ID 47; nominated by Richard Holm, Jr. and Lawrence Kingsbury

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts date the tower and cabin to 1934, and Forest Lookouts says the tower was erected in 1934; HABS dates the privy to 1934 and the tower to 1935, and NHLR also says 1935. This story follows HABS.
HABS gives the log cabin as 1936-37; NHLR gives 1936. Both are shown.

notes_for_editor: Original-site description rests on the 1996 HABS report; no source describes the site after 1996 apart from the NHLR cabin fire in 2000. The NHLR gives Borlaug's Nobel year as 1974; the story does not repeat the year. Outside the sources read, the Nobel Peace Prize he won was in 1970, so the NHLR year looks wrong and should be checked before any year is added. The moved-tower record us-id-cold-mountain-at-payette-lake-holm covers the same tower, so this story leads with the original site and carries the move.
